id: title:danielcarletti:snowflake 403 message covers expired result urls

review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion reliability and recovery from transient access-denied failures in Snowflake connectors.
review.reason: The change distinguishes between persistent access-denied 403 errors and transient 403s caused by expired result-chunk URLs after long-running Snowflake syncs. P1.F1.H1 implements the conditional retry classification, P1.F1.H2 clarifies the distinction between this and budget exhaustion, and P1.F2.H1 adds regression tests. This could allow recovery from transient ingestion failures
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on the frequency of expired-result-chunk 403s in production, which is not established by the code. The tier is assigned based on the implementation of a bounded, substantive reliability improvement rather than unverified adoption or systemic risk reduction.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Replaces a blanket classification of HTTP 403 as non-retryable with a conditional classification: persistent access-denied 403 remains non-retryable, while 403s occurring after long-running syncs are treated as potentially transient (expired result-chunk URLs) and thus retryable.
observations.code_quote: "HTTP 403: Forbidden": "Snowflake refused a request with an HTTP 403 (forbidden). If the sync ran for several hours before failing, the temporary link Snowflake gave us to download the query results expired. Resync to get a fresh one. If it failed soon after starting, check your Snowflake role grants and network access rules, then resync.",
observations.posthog_connection: Changes warehouse ingestion reliability by distinguishing between transient and persistent access-denied failures, potentially allowing recovery from expired result-chunk URLs without manual intervention.

observations.behavior: Updates a comment to clarify that the connector's download retry budget exhaustion is not the same as the access-denied 403 case, distinguishing the two failure modes.
observations.code_quote: # budget is exhausted (`result_batch.py::_download`). Unlike the access-denied 403 case
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies implementation distinction between transient and persistent 403 errors, supporting the new classification logic.

observations.behavior: Updates a test name and assertion to check that both access-denied and expired-result-chunk causes are classified as non-retryable, and that the returned messages contain both "expired" and "grants" keywords.
observations.code_quote: assert all(message is not None and "expired" in message and "grants" in message for message in messages)
observations.posthog_connection: Adds regression checks for the new dual-classification behavior, ensuring both transient and persistent 403 cases are handled and distinguished.
